concerns: Minor, non-blocking: `RecordValue::Str` is used for three fields -- `ts`, `kernel`, `note`. `note` is unambiguously free text (no anti-pattern #7 concern). `kernel` is an open-ended name, not a closed vocabulary, so String is the right shape (an Ident closed-set would be wrong here since kernel names aren't enumerable). `ts`, however, is described as 'string (RFC3339 shape)' and 'shape-validated only' (§1.4) -- this is genuinely structured data (a timestamp) represented as an unparsed string with only shallow shape validation, which sits closer to the anti-pattern #7 line than `kernel`/`note` do. It is a defensible minimal-build cut (no chrono/date type exists elsewhere in the grammar, and full RFC3339 parsing is out of scope for an annotation schema), but the spec should say explicitly that 'shape-validated' does not mean 'semantically validated' (e.g. `9999-99-99T99:99:99.000Z` shape-matches but is not a real instant) so the coder doesn't over- or under-build the validator.

Sitting exactly at the AT-2925 ceiling with zero declared slack (§8's closing line: 'at the AT-2925 ceiling (<= AT-2925 held)') is acceptable -- there is no collision risk since AT-2926+ is genuinely unclaimed by any other milestone -- but it does mean QA/coder has no numbering headroom if a gap is found during implementation (e.g. a missed reject fixture); the next ID would be AT-2926, which is fine today but is a razor's edge compared to M3.18's explicit 'ceiling <= AT-2900 honored' buffer language. Worth a one-line note in the coder handoff that a genuinely necessary new AT should just take AT-2926 rather than be shoehorned into an existing ID's fixture list.

§1.4a's forward-compat rule is well-specified for version>1 unknown *keys*, but doesn't fully state what happens if a *known* field under version>1 has a value that is well-typed at the RecordValue level (e.g. an Ident) but the specific ident is outside v1's closed set for that field (e.g. a new `unit` ident a v2 writer introduces) -- §1.4a's last row says this 'is a breaking change out of v1's forward-compat scope' and 'will reject,' which is internally consistent and correctly conservative, just worth flagging as the one edge where forward-compat intentionally does NOT save the older compiler (by design, and correctly so, but a coder skimming only the table headers could miss it).

summary: APPROVE (r2). Every must-fix and should-fix claimed as closed was independently re-verified against the actual tree this pass, not taken on the architect's word: the rewrite_verify::Verdict enum really is 6 variants matching the spec's corrected vocabulary and mapping table; DESIGN.md's highest numbered subsection really is 3.1.42, making 3.1.43 the correct next slot (not r1's off-by-one 3.1.44); no RecordValue/RecordField naming collision exists in the current parser AST; and AT-2900..2925 (including the r2-added AT-2919..2925 hardening range) is collision-free repo-wide. The closed, non-recursive RecordValue{Str|Int|Ident} enum together with the §1.3a EBNF genuinely closes the pessimistic reviewer's grammar-forever hole -- nested records/calls/holes are structurally unrepresentable, not just parser-rejected by convention -- and the writer fail-closed-at-cap plus the version/forward-compat preserve-and-warn rule are both specified with exact, testable state tables appropriate for a schema that will live embedded in source across compiler versions. The Str/Ident split in RecordValue is appropriately scoped against anti-pattern #7: closed-vocabulary concepts (unit, verdict) are Ident-enum-validated, while genuinely open data (kernel name, free-text note) stays String; the one soft spot is `ts`, which is structured data validated only at shape-level -- a defensible minimal-build cut but worth one clarifying line so the coder doesn't over/under-build RFC3339 validation. Sitting exactly at the AT-2925 ceiling with zero numbering slack is fine (AT-2926+ is genuinely unclaimed) but is worth flagging as a note for QA/coder, not a defect. No concern in this pass rises above minor/non-blocking; none requires another revision cycle.
